MAJAZ:v1p14/r7.author: Abū ʿUbayda Maʿmar b. al-Muthannā
MAJAZ:v1p14/r7.speaker: author
MAJAZ:v1p14/r7.claim: The particle أم is explained as بل, ‘rather’: ‘Rather, I am better.’
MAJAZ:v1p14/r7.anchor: «هذه الأنهار تجري من تحتي أفلا تبصرون أم أنا خير من هذا الذي هو مهين» (43/ 51، 52) معناه: بل أنا خير.

ASAD-NOTES:43:51#n42/r1.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:43:51#n42/r1.speaker: author
ASAD-NOTES:43:51#n42/r1.claim: Pharaoh's claim that the waters were beneath him means they were at his command, referring to the Nile irrigation network controlled by royal power.
ASAD-NOTES:43:51#n42/r1.anchor: a reference to the imposing irrigation system originating in the Nile and controlled by royal power

ELMALILI:43:46-56/r1.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:43:46-56/r1.speaker: author
ELMALILI:43:46-56/r1.claim: Quraysh undervalued the Prophet because he lacked worldly wealth, as Pharaoh boasted of Egypt against Moses; this story consoles and strengthens the Prophet and warns his opponents.
ELMALILI:43:46-56/r1.anchor: Firavun da Hazret-i Mûsâ’ya karşı أَلَيْسَ لِى مُلْكُ مِصْرَ diye öyle gururlanmıştı

ELMALILI:43:46-56/r3.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:43:46-56/r3.speaker: author
ELMALILI:43:46-56/r3.claim: The story also contains subtleties not found in its tellings elsewhere.
ELMALILI:43:46-56/r3.anchor: Bununla beraber nefs-i kıssada da diğer yerlerde bulunmayan nükteler dahi eksik değildir.

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:43:45/r1.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:43:45/r1.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:43:45/r1.claim: The account of Moses’ confrontation with Pharaoh and his people supplies historical lessons within the Prophet’s call and struggle for tawhid.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:43:45/r1.anchor: Buradaki örnek Hz. Mûsâ ile Mısır’ın tanrı kralı Firavun ve tebaası arasında geçen olaylar, tartışmalar ve alınan ibretlik sonuçlardır.

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:43:45/r2.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:43:45/r2.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:43:45/r2.claim: Unbelievers retain a deep belief in God that worldly incentives and suggestions bury; disasters sent in mercy revive it, but they return to denial when hardship passes.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:43:45/r2.anchor: İnkârcıların bilinçlerinin derinliklerinde bir Allah inancı vardır, çeşitli telkinler ve dünyanın çekici menfaatleri bu temel duyguyu köreltmiş veya üstünü küllerle örtmüştür.

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:43:45/r3.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:43:45/r3.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:43:45/r3.claim: Tawhid is every prophet’s shared message: scripture and its remnants show that God never permitted worship of another being, as Moses’ struggle also proves.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:43:45/r3.anchor: Tevhid inancı bütün peygamberlerin ortak tebliğleri ve inanç ilkeleridir. Kendilerine kitap gönderilmiş topluluklara sorulduğunda veya eski kitapların kalıntıları okunduğunda anlaşılmaktadır ki, Allah hiçbir zaman kendisi dışında bir varlığa kulluk edilmesine izin vermemiştir.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-7-english:p170/r6.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-7-english:p170/r6.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-7-english:p170/r6.claim: Moses and Jesus both called people to monotheism; Pharaoh and his chiefs rejected Moses' successive signs for the same arrogant reason as Quraysh and met their deserved fate, which Quraysh will also face.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-7-english:p170/r6.anchor: Moses (sws) showed great signs one after the other to the Pharaoh and his chiefs

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-7-english:p171/r4.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-7-english:p171/r4.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-7-english:p171/r4.claim: Every part of Sūrah al-Zukhruf relates deeply to its central theme, and the whole sūrah forms a harmonious unit from beginning to end.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-7-english:p171/r4.anchor: each part of it is deeply related to its central theme

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-7-english:p199/r4.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-7-english:p199/r4.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-7-english:p199/r4.claim: Pharaoh proclaimed his possession of Egypt and its canals as Moses' miracles and arguments shook his people's devotion; the author compares this to Quraysh leaders' objection about the Qur'an's recipient.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-7-english:p199/r4.anchor: he made an announcement among his people that the kingdom of Egypt and its running canals are in his possession

BURSEVI:v8p290#2/r1.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v8p290#2/r1.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v8p290#2/r1.claim: Pharaoh called out in the assembly himself or through a herald after the punishment lifted, fearing the people would believe.
BURSEVI:v8p290#2/r1.anchor: ونادى فرعون} بنفسه أو بمناد أمره بالنداء {فى قومه} في مجمعهم وفيما بينهم

BURSEVI:v8p290#2/r2.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v8p290#2/r2.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v8p290#2/r2.claim: The source characterizes Pharaoh’s speech as boastful and proud; “my people” addresses the Copts.
BURSEVI:v8p290#2/r2.anchor: قال} : (كفت از روى عظمت وافتخار). يا قوم} : (اى كروه من يعنى قبطيان).

BURSEVI:v8p290#2/r3.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v8p290#2/r3.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v8p290#2/r3.claim: The author describes Egypt as forty farsakhs by forty.

BURSEVI:v8p290#2/r4.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v8p290#2/r4.speaker: الكاشفي
BURSEVI:v8p290#2/r4.claim: Al-Kāshifī gives the extent of Egypt as from Alexandria to the Syrian border.
BURSEVI:v8p290#2/r4.anchor: قال الكاشفي : (آيانيست مرا مملكت مصر از اسكندريه تاسر حد شام).

BURSEVI:v8p290#2/r5.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v8p290#2/r5.speaker: فتح الرحمن
BURSEVI:v8p290#2/r5.claim: Fatḥ al-Raḥmān describes Egypt as extending roughly from Alexandria to Aswan along the Nile.
BURSEVI:v8p290#2/r5.anchor: وفي "فتح الرحمن" : وهو من نحو الإسنكدرية إلى أسوان بطول النيل.

BURSEVI:v8p290#2/r6.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v8p290#2/r6.speaker: القاموس
BURSEVI:v8p290#2/r6.claim: Al-Qāmūs identifies Aswan as a town in Upper Egypt.
BURSEVI:v8p290#2/r6.anchor: وأسوان بالضم : بلد بصعيد مصر كما في "القاموس".

BURSEVI:v8p290#2/r7.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v8p290#2/r7.speaker: روضة الأخبار
BURSEVI:v8p290#2/r7.claim: Rawḍat al-Akhbār says Egypt was built by Miṣr, son of Ḥām, son of Noah, and named after him.
BURSEVI:v8p290#2/r7.anchor: قال في"روضة الأخبار" : مصر بلدة معروفة بناها مصر بن حام بن نوح.

BURSEVI:v8p290#2/r8.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v8p290#2/r8.speaker: القاموس
BURSEVI:v8p290#2/r8.claim: Al-Qāmūs derives the city’s name either from becoming urbanized or from its builder, Miṣr son of Noah.
BURSEVI:v8p290#2/r8.anchor: وفي "القاموس" : مصر والمكان تمصيرا جعلوه مصرا ، فتمصر ، ومصر للمدينة المعروفة

BURSEVI:v8p290#2/r9.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v8p290#2/r9.speaker: بعضهم
BURSEVI:v8p290#2/r9.claim: Another etymology connects Miṣr with the verb “to cut”: the city was separated from open land by its buildings.
BURSEVI:v8p290#2/r9.anchor: وقال بعضهم : مصر بلد معروف من مصر الشيء يمصره إذا قطعه سمي به لانقطاعه عن الفضاء بالعمارة.

BURSEVI:v8p290#3/r1.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v8p290#3/r1.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v8p290#3/r1.claim: “These rivers” means channels of the Nile; the definite article stands in place of a possessive phrase.
BURSEVI:v8p290#3/r1.anchor: وهاذه الانهار} ؛ أي : أنهار النيل ، فاللام عوض عن المضاف إليه.

BURSEVI:v8p290#3/r2.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v8p290#3/r2.speaker: كشف الأسرار
BURSEVI:v8p290#3/r2.claim: Kashf al-asrar says Nile water is divided into 360 channels.
BURSEVI:v8p290#3/r2.anchor: قال في "كشف الأسرار" : (آب نيل بسيصد وشصت جوى منقسم بوده).

BURSEVI:v8p290#3/r3.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v8p290#3/r3.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v8p290#3/r3.claim: The intended rivers are major Nile branches, principally four: the Malik or Alexandria canal, Tulun, Damietta, and Tinnīs; Tinnīs was on an island near Damietta and was famed for fine textiles.
BURSEVI:v8p290#3/r3.anchor: والمراد هنا : الخلجان الكبار الخارجة من النيل ومعظمها أربعة أنهر : نهر الملك ، وهو نهر الإسكندرية

BURSEVI:v8p290#3/r4.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v8p290#3/r4.speaker: القاموس
BURSEVI:v8p290#3/r4.claim: Al-Qāmūs locates Tinnīs on an island near Damietta and notes its fine fabrics.
BURSEVI:v8p290#3/r4.anchor: وهو كسكين بلد بجزيرة من جزائر بحر الروم قرب دمياط ينسب إليها الثياب الفاخرة كما في "القاموس".

BURSEVI:v8p290#3/r5.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v8p290#3/r5.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v8p290#3/r5.claim: “They flow beneath me” means either below Pharaoh’s palace or beneath his command.

BURSEVI:v8p290#3/r6.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v8p290#3/r6.speaker: الكاشفي
BURSEVI:v8p290#3/r6.claim: Al-Kāshifī says four great streams ran through Pharaoh’s garden and below his palaces.
BURSEVI:v8p290#3/r6.anchor: قال الكاشفي : (جهار حوى بزرك درباغ او ميرفت واز زير قصر هاى او ميكذست).

BURSEVI:v8p290#3/r7.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v8p290#3/r7.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v8p290#3/r7.claim: The waw may coordinate the rivers with the kingdom, making “they flow” circumstantial, or introduce a circumstantial clause whose subject is “these rivers.”
BURSEVI:v8p290#3/r7.anchor: والواو إما عاطفة لهذه الأنهار على ملك ، فتجري حال منها ، أو للحال فهذه مبتدأ

BURSEVI:v8p290#3/r8.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v8p290#3/r8.speaker: خريدة العجائب
BURSEVI:v8p290#3/r8.claim: Kharīdat al-ʿAjāʾib claims no river is longer than the Nile and describes its course as two months in Muslim lands, two in unbelieving lands, two in wilderness, and four in ruined territory.
BURSEVI:v8p290#3/r8.anchor: قال في "خريدة العجائب" : ليس في الدنيا نهر أطول من النيل ؛ لأن مسيرته شهران في الإسلام ،

BURSEVI:v8p290#3/r9.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v8p290#3/r9.speaker: خريدة العجائب
BURSEVI:v8p290#3/r9.claim: The same source places the Nile’s source at the Mountain of the Moon beyond the equator and says it emerges from the Sea of Darkness, the Black Sea, before entering below that mountain.
BURSEVI:v8p290#3/r9.anchor: ومخرجه من بلاد جبل القمر خلف خط الاستواء ، وسمي جبل القمر ؛ لأن القمر لا يطلع عليه أصلا

BURSEVI:v8p290#3/r10.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v8p290#3/r10.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v8p290#3/r10.claim: The only river comparable to the Nile is the Mehran, the Indus.
BURSEVI:v8p290#3/r10.anchor: وليس في الدنيا نهر يشبه بالنيل إلا نهر مهران ، وهو نهر السند.

BURSEVI:v8p290#4/r1.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v8p290#4/r1.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v8p290#4/r1.claim: Pharaoh’s “will you not see?” expresses his exaltation of and pride in his kingdom.
BURSEVI:v8p290#4/r1.anchor: أفلا تبصرون} : ذلك يريد به استعظام ملكه

BURSEVI:v8p290#4/r2.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v8p290#4/r2.speaker: هارون الرشيد
BURSEVI:v8p290#4/r2.claim: When Hārūn al-Rashīd read the verse, he vowed to give Egypt to his least worthy servant and appointed al-Khaṣīb, his bath attendant.
BURSEVI:v8p290#4/r2.anchor: وعن هارون الرشيد لما قرأها قال : لأولينها أخس عبيدي ، فولاها الخصيب

BURSEVI:v8p290#4/r3.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v8p290#4/r3.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v8p290#4/r3.claim: The story calls al-Khaṣīb black and foolish; when farmers complained that untimely rain ruined their millet beside the Nile, he foolishly said they should have waited to plant it.
BURSEVI:v8p290#4/r3.anchor: وكان أسود أحمق. (عقل وكفايت آن سياه بحدى بودكه طائفة حراث مصر شكايت آور

BURSEVI:v8p290#4/r4.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v8p290#4/r4.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v8p290#4/r4.claim: The accompanying Persian couplet says greater knowledge does not guarantee greater worldly fortune: the ignorant may prosper so much that the learned are astonished.
BURSEVI:v8p290#4/r4.anchor: اكر روزى بدانش برفزودى زنادان تنك روزى تر نبودى بنادانان جنان روزى رساند

BURSEVI:v8p290#4/r5.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v8p290#4/r5.speaker: عبد الله بن طاهر
BURSEVI:v8p290#4/r5.claim: ʿAbd Allāh ibn Ṭāhir refused to enter Egypt, saying it was too small to merit the place where Pharaoh boasted of his kingdom.
BURSEVI:v8p290#4/r5.anchor: وعن عبد الله بن طاهر أنه وليها ، فخرج إليها ، فلما شارفها ، ووقع عليها بصره. قال : أهي القرية التي افتخر فيها فرعون

BURSEVI:v8p290#4/r6.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v8p290#4/r6.speaker: ابن الفرج بن الجوزي
BURSEVI:v8p290#4/r6.claim: Ibn al-Faraj ibn al-Jawzī calls Pharaoh pitiable for boasting of a river whose flow he did not produce.
BURSEVI:v8p290#4/r6.anchor: قال الحافظ ابن الفرج بن الجوزي يوما في قول فرعون : وهذه الأنهار تجري من تحتي ، ويحه افتخر بنهر ما أجراه

BURSEVI:v8p290#4/r7.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v8p290#4/r7.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v8p290#4/r7.claim: A Persian couplet says pride in color, scent, and place is childish joy and deception.
BURSEVI:v8p290#4/r7.anchor: افتخار از رنك وبو وازمكان هست شادى وفريب كودكان

QIRAAT-ER:43:51:18#1/r1.author: QIRAAT-ER
QIRAAT-ER:43:51:18#1/r1.speaker: author
QIRAAT-ER:43:51:18#1/r1.claim: The yāʾ variant opens the final possessive sound as taḥtiya instead of pausing on taḥtī.
QIRAAT-ER:43:51:18#1/r1.anchor: opens the final possessive sound as taḥtiya instead of pausing on taḥtī

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p378/r1.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p378/r1.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p378/r1.claim: The story of Pharaoh follows Quraysh's demand that revelation go to a wealthy notable: Pharaoh also boasted of Egypt's rule, yet Moses overcame him, as will happen to Quraysh.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p378/r1.anchor: اختيارهم أن ينزل القرآن على رجل من القريتين عظيم

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p381/r5.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p381/r5.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p381/r5.claim: The call likely addressed Egypts elite at their meeting place, with Pharaoh raising his voice so his words spread.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p381/r5.anchor: والظاهر أنه نادى عظماء القبط في محله الذي هو وهم يجتمعون فيه

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p381/r6.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p381/r6.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p381/r6.claim: The Nile channels Pharaoh named included the River of the King, Tulun, Damietta, and Tinnis.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p381/r6.anchor: وأعظمها: نهر الملك، ونهر طولون، ونهر دمياط، ونهر تنيس

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p381/r8.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p381/r8.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p381/r8.claim: Pharaoh made his people the audience of the call, apparently addressing Egypt's elite at their meeting place and raising his voice so the message would spread.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p381/r8.anchor: والظاهر أنه نادى عظماء القبط في محله الذي هو وهم يجتمعون فيه

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p381/r9.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p381/r9.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p381/r9.claim: The call could also be attributed to Pharaoh because he ordered someone to proclaim it.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p381/r9.anchor: ويجوز أن يكون أمر بالنداء، فأسند إليه

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p381/r10.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p381/r10.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p381/r10.claim: Pharaoh feared the people's allegiance to Moses after seeing God answer Moses' prayer and lift the punishment.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p381/r10.anchor: أنه لما رأى إجابة الله دعوة موسى ورفع العذاب، خاف ميل القوم إليه

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p381/r11.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p381/r11.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p381/r11.claim: Pharaoh's kingdom of Egypt extended from Alexandria to Aswan.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p381/r12.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p381/r12.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p381/r12.claim: The rivers are interpreted as branches or channels of the Nile.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p381/r12.anchor: وهذه الأنهار: أي الخلجان التي تجري من النيل

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p381/r13.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p381/r13.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p381/r13.claim: The waw in “and these rivers” introduces a circumstantial clause; “these rivers” is an adjective or apposition, though coordination with “kingdom” is also possible.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p381/r13.anchor: والواو في وهذه الأنهار واو الحال، وتجري خبر

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p381/r14.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p381/r14.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p381/r14.claim: “From beneath me” means beneath Pharaoh's control and rule.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p381/r14.anchor: من تحتي: أي من تحت قهري وملكي

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p381/r15.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p381/r15.speaker: قتادة
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p381/r15.claim: Qatada says Pharaoh's gardens and rivers flowed beneath his palace.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p381/r15.anchor: وقال قتادة: كانت جنانها وأنهارها تجري من تحت قصره

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p381/r16.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p381/r16.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p381/r16.claim: Another view says Pharaoh had a great throne and diverted part of the Nile into channels flowing beneath it.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p381/r16.anchor: وقيل: كان له سرير عظيم، وقطع من نيل مصر قطعة قسمها أنهارا

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p381/r17.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p381/r17.speaker: الضحاك
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p381/r17.claim: Al-Dahhak interprets the rivers as commanders and powerful chiefs marching under Pharaoh's banner; Abu Hayyan calls this interpretation far-fetched.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p381/r17.anchor: وأبعد الضحاك في تفسيره الأنهار بالقواد والرؤساء الجبابرة

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p381/r18.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p381/r18.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p381/r18.claim: Some interpret the rivers as wealth, which Pharaoh controlled.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p381/r18.anchor: ومن فسرها بالأموال، يعرفها من تحت يده

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p381/r19.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p381/r19.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p381/r19.claim: Some interpret them as horses, since a horse can also be called a river.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p381/r19.anchor: ومن فسرها بالخيل فقيل: كما سمي الفرس بحرا يسمى نهرا

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p381/r20.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p381/r20.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p381/r20.claim: Abu Hayyan says the interpretations of rivers as leaders, wealth, or horses resemble esoteric exegesis.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p381/r20.anchor: وهذه الأقوال الثلاثة تقرب من تفاسير الباطنية

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p381/r21.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p381/r21.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p381/r21.claim: Pharaoh's rhetorical question boasts of his greatness and power while belittling Moses as helpless.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p381/r21.anchor: أفلا تبصرون عظمتي وقدرتي وعجز موسى

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p381/r22.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p381/r22.speaker: مهدي بن الصفير
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p381/r22.claim: Mahdi ibn al-Sufayr reads يبصرون with the third-person yāʾ.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p381/r22.anchor: وقرأ مهدي بن الصفير: يبصرون، بياء الغيبة

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p381#2/r1.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p381#2/r1.speaker: عيسى
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p381#2/r1.claim: Isa reads أفلا تبصرون with a kasra on the nūn.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p381#2/r2.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p381#2/r2.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p381#2/r2.claim: Anecdote: al-Rashid read the verse, promised Egypt to his best servant, and appointed al-Khasib, who was performing ablution.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p381#2/r2.anchor: وعن الرشيد، أنه لما قرأها قال: لأولينها أحسن عبيدي

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p381#2/r3.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p381#2/r3.speaker: عبد الله بن طاهر
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p381#2/r3.claim: Abdullah ibn Tahir turned back rather than enter Egypt, saying it was too insignificant for him despite being the land Pharaoh had boasted of.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p381#2/r3.anchor: أهي القرية التي افتخر بها فرعون حتى قال: أليس لي ملك مصر؟

QUSHAYRI:v3p177/r8.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v3p177/r8.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v3p177/r8.claim: Pharaoh boasted of his Egyptian kingdom and the Nile running beneath him, and this became his ruin; whoever exalts himself through anything besides God will find destruction in that very thing.
QUSHAYRI:v3p177/r8.anchor: تعزز بملك مصر ، وجري النيل بأمره ! وكان في ذلك هلاكه ؛ ليعلم أن من تعزز بشيء من دون الله فحتفه وهلاكه في ذلك الشيء

ALUSI-FULL:v25p89/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v25p89/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v25p89/r1.claim: Pharaoh may have raised his own voice among his people, perhaps gathering Coptic notables at his residence after the punishment lifted to spread his boast and deter belief in Moses.
ALUSI-FULL:v25p89/r1.anchor: رفع صوته بنفسه فيما بين قومه بذلك القول ولعله جمع عظماءالقبط في محله الذي هو فيه بعد أن كشف العذاب

ALUSI-FULL:v25p89/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v25p89/r2.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v25p89/r2.claim: Alternatively, the call is figuratively attributed to Pharaoh because he ordered public criers to proclaim it in markets, lanes, and gathering places.
ALUSI-FULL:v25p89/r2.anchor: ويجوز أن يكون إسناد النداء إليه مجازا والمراد أمر بالنداء بذلك في الأسواق والأزقة ومجاميع الناس

ALUSI-FULL:v25p89/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v25p89/r3.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v25p89/r3.claim: The construction treats the call as deeply established among them, with a poetic comparison for a verb made intransitive and then extended.
ALUSI-FULL:v25p89/r3.anchor: قل معطوف على فاجأ المقدر ونزل منزلة اللازم وعدي وبقي كقوله : يجرح في عراقيبها نصلي

ALUSI-FULL:v25p89/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v25p89/r4.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v25p89/r4.claim: His ملك مصر means authority to govern and administer Egypt, not the land alone; the territory extended from Alexandria to Aswan.
ALUSI-FULL:v25p89/r4.anchor: وعندي بملك مصر ضبطها والتعرف فيها بالحكم ولم يرد مصر نفسها بل هي ومايتبعها وذلك من اسكندرية إلى أسوان

ALUSI-FULL:v25p89/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v25p89/r5.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v25p89/r5.claim: The rivers are channels branching from the Nile, including the Canal of the King, Damietta, and Tanis; the Ibn Ṭūlūn canal may have existed then but was later restored by Aḥmad ibn Ṭūlūn.
ALUSI-FULL:v25p89/r5.anchor: والأنهار الخلجان التي تخرج من النيل المبارك كنهر الملك ونهر دمياط ونهر تنيس

ALUSI-FULL:v25p89/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v25p89/r6.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v25p89/r6.claim: من تحتي means under my command.
ALUSI-FULL:v25p89/r6.anchor: وأراد بقوله ( من تحتي ) من تحت أمري

ALUSI-FULL:v25p89/r7.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v25p89/r7.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v25p89/r7.claim: Another view says streams flowed from the Nile under Pharaoh's palace or under a raised throne overlooking them.
ALUSI-FULL:v25p89/r7.anchor: وقال غير واحد كانت أنهار تخرج من النيل وتجري من تحت قصره وهو مشرف عليها

ALUSI-FULL:v25p89/r8.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v25p89/r8.speaker: قتادة
ALUSI-FULL:v25p89/r8.claim: Qatāda interprets the rivers as gardens and orchards in front of Pharaoh through which streams ran.
ALUSI-FULL:v25p89/r8.anchor: وقال قتادة : كانت له جنان وبساتين بين يديه تجري فيها الأنهار

ALUSI-FULL:v25p89/r9.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v25p89/r9.speaker: الضحاك
ALUSI-FULL:v25p89/r9.claim: Al-Ḍaḥḥāk interprets the rivers as powerful chiefs who marched beneath Pharaoh's banner and obeyed his orders.
ALUSI-FULL:v25p89/r9.anchor: وفسره الضحاك الأنهار بالقواد الرؤساء الجبابرة ومعنى كونهم يجرون من تحته أنهم يسيرون تحت لوائه

ALUSI-FULL:v25p89/r10.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v25p89/r10.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v25p89/r10.claim: The author calls al-Ḍaḥḥāk's interpretation far-fetched and rejects the further readings of rivers as wealth or horses as esoteric interpretations.
ALUSI-FULL:v25p89/r10.anchor: وقد أبعد جدا وكذا من فسرها بالأموال ومن فسرها بالخيل

ALUSI-FULL:v25p89/r11.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v25p89/r11.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v25p89/r11.claim: The واو in وهذه may coordinate the rivers with ملك, with تجري as a circumstantial clause, or mark a circumstantial clause whose subject is هذه and whose predicate is الأنهار تجري.
ALUSI-FULL:v25p89/r11.anchor: والواو في ( وهذه ) الخ إما عاطفة لهه الأنهار على الملك فجملة تجري حال منها أو للحال فهذه مبتدأ

ALUSI-FULL:v25p89/r12.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v25p89/r12.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v25p89/r12.claim: A further syntax makes هذه تجري a subject-predicate clause coordinated with the predicate of ليس.
ALUSI-FULL:v25p89/r12.anchor: وجوز أن تكون للعطف وهذه تجري مبتدأ وخبر والجملة عطف على اسم ليس وخبرها

ALUSI-FULL:v25p89#2/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v25p89#2/r1.speaker: عيسى
ALUSI-FULL:v25p89#2/r1.claim: ʿĪsā reads تبصرون with kasra on nūn and an omitted yāʾ object.
ALUSI-FULL:v25p89#2/r1.anchor: وقرأ عيسى تبصرون بكسر النون فتكون الياء الواقعة مفعولا لا وحذوفة

ALUSI-FULL:v25p89#2/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v25p89#2/r2.speaker: فهد بن القصر
ALUSI-FULL:v25p89#2/r2.claim: Fahd ibn al-Qaṣr reads the verb in the third person as يبصرون.
ALUSI-FULL:v25p89#2/r2.anchor: وقرأ فهد بن القصر يبصرون بياء الغيبة ذكره في الكامل للهزلي

ALUSI-FULL:v25p89#2/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v25p89#2/r3.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v25p89#2/r3.claim: تبصرون either has an implied object, meaning the matter just mentioned, or is intransitive, asking whether they have sight or insight.
ALUSI-FULL:v25p89#2/r3.anchor: على تقدير المفعول أي أفلا تبصرون ذلك أي ما ذكر ويجوز أن ينزل منزلة اللازم والمعنى أليس لكم بصر أو بصيرة

ALUSI-FULL:v25p89#2/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v25p89#2/r4.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v25p89#2/r4.claim: There is a striking distance between Pharaoh's boast of Egyptian kingship and his claim to divinity.
ALUSI-FULL:v25p89#2/r4.anchor: ولا يخفى ما بين افتخار اللعين بملك مصر ودعواه الربوبية من البعد البعيد

ALUSI-FULL:v25p89#2/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v25p89#2/r5.speaker: الرشيد
ALUSI-FULL:v25p89#2/r5.claim: Al-Rashid reportedly vowed to give Egypt to his least servant after hearing the verse and gave it to al-Khaṣīb, his ablutions attendant.
ALUSI-FULL:v25p89#2/r5.anchor: وعن الرشيد أنه لما قال هذه الآية قال : لأولينها يعني مصر أخس عبيدي فولاها الخصيب وكان على وضوئه

ALUSI-FULL:v25p89#2/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v25p89#2/r6.speaker: عبد الله ابن طاهر
ALUSI-FULL:v25p89#2/r6.claim: When appointed Egypt's governor, ʿAbd Allah ibn Ṭāhir saw it from afar, called it a village Pharaoh had boasted of, and turned his reins away rather than enter.
ALUSI-FULL:v25p89#2/r6.anchor: وعن عبد الله ابن طاهر أنه وليها فخرج إليها فلما شارفها ووقع عليها بصره قال : هي القرية التي أفتخر بها فرعون

BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p217/r2.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p217/r2.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p217/r2.claim: Pharaoh boasts that the Nile’s rivers flow beneath his palaces and asks whether his people can see his greatness and powerful rule.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p217/r2.anchor: وهذه الأنهار} أنهار النيل، {تجري من تحتي} من تحت قصوري

BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p217/r3.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p217/r3.speaker: قتادة
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p217/r3.claim: Qatada interprets the rivers flowing beneath Pharaoh as flowing before him in his gardens and orchards.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p217/r3.anchor: وقال قتادة: تجري بين يدي في جناني وبساتيني.

BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p217/r4.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p217/r4.speaker: الحسن
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p217/r4.claim: Hasan interprets the rivers’ flowing as occurring by Pharaoh’s command.

BAYDAWI-FULL:43:49-51/r7.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:43:49-51/r7.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:43:49-51/r7.claim: Pharaoh called out personally or through a herald, in the assembly or among his people after the punishment was lifted, fearing some might believe.
BAYDAWI-FULL:43:49-51/r7.anchor: بنفسه أو بمناديه. { في قومه } في مجمعهم أو فيما بينهم بعد كشف العذاب عنهم مخافة أن يؤمن بعضهم

BAYDAWI-FULL:43:49-51/r8.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:43:49-51/r8.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:43:49-51/r8.claim: The rivers are Nile’s branches, chiefly four: the River of the King, Ṭūlūn, Damietta, and Tanīs.
BAYDAWI-FULL:43:49-51/r8.anchor: أنهار النيل ومعظمها أربعة أنهر: نهر الملك، ونهر طولون، ونهر دمياط، ونهر تنيس

BAYDAWI-FULL:43:49-51/r9.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:43:49-51/r9.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:43:49-51/r9.claim: ‘Flow beneath me’ means beneath his palace or authority, or in front of him in his gardens.
BAYDAWI-FULL:43:49-51/r9.anchor: تحت قصري أو أمري، أو بين يدي في جناني

BAYDAWI-FULL:43:49-51/r10.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:43:49-51/r10.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:43:49-51/r10.claim: The waw either coordinates the rivers with the kingdom and ‘flow’ is their circumstantial clause, or it is a circumstantial waw introducing ‘these rivers’ as subject, with ‘flow’ as predicate.
BAYDAWI-FULL:43:49-51/r10.anchor: والواو إما عاطفة لهذه { الأنهر } على الملك و { تجرى } حال منها

BAYDAWI-FULL:43:49-51/r11.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:43:49-51/r11.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:43:49-51/r11.claim: Pharaoh challenges his people to see his claimed power and wealth.
BAYDAWI-FULL:43:49-51/r11.anchor: الأنهر } صفتها و { تجرى } خبرها. { أفلا تبصرون } ذلك

BIQAI-FULL:v7p35/r9.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v7p35/r9.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v7p35/r9.claim: Beyond breaking his word, Pharaoh summons his people to spread his message widely so no one thinks he has converted; he fears the signs have shaken their hearts.
BIQAI-FULL:v7p35/r9.anchor: أي الذين لهم غاية القيام معه

BIQAI-FULL:v7p35/r10.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v7p35/r10.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v7p35/r10.claim: Pharaoh appeals to common identity and their strength, then claims that his exclusive rule over Egypt leaves no one entitled to challenge him.
BIQAI-FULL:v7p35/r10.anchor: بأنهم لحمة واحدة , ومستنهضا بوصفهم بأنهم ذوو قوة على ما يحاولونه

BIQAI-FULL:v7p35/r11.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v7p35/r11.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v7p35/r11.claim: Pharaoh portrays Israel's departure from his control as rebellion against the rightful ruler and disorder, excusing his broken pledge under pressure.
BIQAI-FULL:v7p35/r11.anchor: أن غلبته على بني إسرائيل ومقاهرته على إخراجهم من تحت يده بغى على من له الملك فتكون فسادا

BIQAI-FULL:v7p35/r12.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v7p35/r12.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v7p35/r12.claim: The reading leaves Miṣr without tanwīn, marking it as a proper name; tanwīn can imply diminishment, contrary to Pharaoh's intended grandeur.
BIQAI-FULL:v7p35/r12.anchor: ولم يقرأ بالصرف ليكون نصا على مراده من العلمية , ولأن المصر يطلق على المدينة الواحدة

BIQAI-FULL:v7p35/r13.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v7p35/r13.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v7p35/r13.claim: Pharaoh says the rivers run beneath him because he had branched canals toward his gardens and palaces and could direct them wherever he wished, a power no one else had.
BIQAI-FULL:v7p35/r13.anchor: من تشقيق الخلجان إلى بساتينه وقصوره

BIQAI-FULL:v7p35/r14.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v7p35/r14.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v7p35/r14.claim: ‘Do you not see?’ asks them to perceive inwardly that no one should rival him; Biqāʿī calls this the speech of a weakened man whose ties have come undone.
BIQAI-FULL:v7p35/r14.anchor: أي الذي ذكرته لكم فتعلموا ببصائر قلوبكم أنه لا ينبغي لأحد أن ينازعني

DURR-FULL:v7p383/r1.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v7p383/r1.speaker: عائشة
DURR-FULL:v7p383/r1.claim: Aisha says political authority belongs to God, who gives it to the virtuous and the wicked; Pharaoh ruled Egypt for four hundred years.
DURR-FULL:v7p383/r1.anchor: عن الأسود بن يزيد قال: قلت لعائشة: ألا تعجبين من رجل من الطلقاء ينازع أصحاب محمد في الخلافة قالت: وما تعجب من ذلك هو سلطان الله يؤتيه البر والفاجر وقد ملك فرعون أهل مصر أربعمائة سنة

DURR-FULL:v7p383/r2.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v7p383/r2.speaker: قتادة
DURR-FULL:v7p383/r2.claim: Pharaoh's claim to own Egypt and its rivers refers to his having gardens and rivers.
DURR-FULL:v7p383/r2.anchor: عن قتادة {أليس لي ملك مصر وهذه الأنهار تجري من تحتي} قال: قد كان لهم جنان وأنهار

IBNASHUR-FULL:v25p228/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v25p228/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v25p228/r1.claim: After the punishment was lifted in response to Moses, Pharaoh and his chiefs broke their promise to accept guidance.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v25p228/r1.anchor: أي تفرع على تضرعهم ووعدهم بالاهتداء إذا كشف عنهم العذاب أنهم نكثوا الوعد

IBNASHUR-FULL:v25p228/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v25p228/r2.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v25p228/r2.claim: Nakth literally means undoing a tightly twisted rope and figuratively means betraying a covenant; the wording recalls the people’s breaking their promise in al-Aʿrāf.

IBNASHUR-FULL:v25p228/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v25p228/r3.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v25p228/r3.claim: The construction here follows the same pattern as the earlier sentence about people laughing at the signs.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v25p228/r3.anchor: والكلام على تركيب هذه الجملة مثل الكلام على قوله آنفا

IBNASHUR-FULL:v25p228/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v25p228/r4.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v25p228/r4.claim: Fearing his people would follow Moses and believe, Pharaoh announced his own greatness to secure obedience and conceal his appeal for the punishment to be lifted, so they would think its end accidental.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v25p228/r4.anchor: خشي فرعون أن يتبع قومه دعوة موسى ويؤمنوا برسالته فأعلن في قومه تذكيرهم بعظمة نفسه

IBNASHUR-FULL:v25p228/r5.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v25p228/r5.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v25p228/r5.claim: The call is a raised voice, but attributing it to Pharaoh is a rational metaphor because he ordered heralds to announce important royal matters publicly.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v25p228/r5.anchor: والنداء : رفع الصوت ، وإسناده إلى فرعون

IBNASHUR-FULL:v25p228/r6.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v25p228/r6.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v25p228/r6.claim: A passage in al-Ḥarīrī’s thirtieth maqāmah illustrates a herald announcing a formal contract.

IBNASHUR-FULL:v25p228/r7.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v25p228/r7.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v25p228/r7.claim: The clause beginning qāla explains nādā, and attributing the speech to Pharaoh uses the same rational metaphor as attributing the call to him.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v25p228/r7.anchor: وجملة { قال } الخ مبينة لجملة { نادى }

IBNASHUR-FULL:v25p228/r8.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v25p228/r8.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v25p228/r8.claim: The Pharaoh depicted in this narrative is identified as Merneptah II.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v25p228/r8.anchor: وفرعون المحكي عنه في هذه القصة هو منفطاح الثاني

IBNASHUR-FULL:v25p229/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v25p229/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v25p229/r1.claim: The rivers are Nile branches and canals, each so large it resembles a river, though they all belong to the single Nile.

IBNASHUR-FULL:v25p229/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v25p229/r2.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v25p229/r2.claim: If Pharaoh’s capital was Memphis, the demonstrative points to the Nile’s two great branches near Cairo, Damietta and Rosetta, forming the Delta.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v25p229/r2.anchor: فإن كان مقر ملك فرعون هذا في مدينة منفيس فاسم الإشارة في قوله

IBNASHUR-FULL:v25p229/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v25p229/r3.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v25p229/r3.claim: On the Memphis reading, one branch may have been called Tanis after the city in that region, which the sea later submerged.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v25p229/r3.anchor: وأحسب أنه الذي كان يدعى فرع تنيس لأن تنيس كانت في تلك الجهة وغمرها البحر

IBNASHUR-FULL:v25p229/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v25p229/r4.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v25p229/r4.claim: If the capital was Thebes near present-day Abu, the demonstrative instead refers to the Nile’s familiar channels and branches visible to local residents.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v25p229/r4.anchor: وإن كان مقر ملكه طيبة التي هي بقرب مدينة آبو اليوم فالإشارة إلى جداول النيل وفروعه المشهورة بين أهل المدينة

IBNASHUR-FULL:v25p229/r5.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v25p229/r5.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v25p229/r5.claim: One reading of beneath me is that the Nile flows at Pharaoh’s command, with beneath serving as a metonym for subjugation, as in the cited phrase about two wives.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v25p229/r5.anchor: أن النيل يجري بأمره ، فيكون { من تحتي } كناية عن التسخير

IBNASHUR-FULL:v25p229/r6.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v25p229/r6.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v25p229/r6.claim: Alternatively, the Nile flows within his kingdom from Aswan to the sea, and beneath metaphorically expresses his control of its course, as on a river reading of the cited verse.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v25p229/r6.anchor: أراد أن النيل يجري في مملكته من بلاد أصوان إلى البحر فيكون في { تحتي } استعارة للتمكن من تصاريف النيل

IBNASHUR-FULL:v25p229/r7.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v25p229/r7.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v25p229/r7.claim: Such a boast could persuade the common people because their understanding was unsophisticated.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v25p229/r7.anchor: وكان مثل هذا الكلام يروج على الدهماء لسذاجة عقولهم

IBNASHUR-FULL:v25p229/r8.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v25p229/r8.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v25p229/r8.claim: A further reading takes the rivers as water outlets supplying the city and gardens, distributed by Pharaoh through dams and reservoirs; he boasts he could cut the water off, like Joseph’s claim about giving full measure.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v25p229/r8.anchor: ويجوز أن يكون المراد بالأنهار مصب المياه التي كانت تسقي المدينة والبساتين التي حولها وأن توزيع المياه كان بأمره

IBNASHUR-FULL:v25p229/r9.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v25p229/r9.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v25p229/r9.claim: On that reading, beneath me means beneath my authority: the water flows only by his order.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v25p229/r9.anchor: فيكون معنى { من تحتي } من تحت أمري أي لا تجري إلا بأمري

IBNASHUR-FULL:v25p229/r10.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v25p229/r10.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v25p229/r10.claim: It is also reported that the rivers ran beneath Pharaoh’s palace.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v25p229/r10.anchor: وقد قيل : كانت الأنهار تجري تحت قصره

IBNASHUR-FULL:v25p229/r11.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v25p229/r11.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v25p229/r11.claim: The question “Do you not see?” is an affirmative rhetorical prompt framed as a negative so the audience is pressed to acknowledge what they see.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v25p229/r11.anchor: والاستفهام في { أفلا تبصرون } تقريري جاء التقرير على النفي تحقيقا لإقرارهم

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p58#2/r1.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p58#2/r1.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p58#2/r1.claim: Pharaoh's proclamation may have been spoken by him in his assembly or announced publicly at his order.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p58#2/r1.anchor: نداء فرعون يحتمل أن يكون بلسانه في ناديه، ويحتمل أن يكون بأن أمر من ينادي في الناس

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p58#2/r2.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p58#2/r2.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p58#2/r2.claim: Pharaoh argues that he is superior to Moses because he rules Egypt and its blessings, while Moses is obscure and poor; if Moses' god were true, He would not leave matters this way.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p58#2/r2.anchor: أنه أراد أن يبين فضله على موسى، إذ هو ملك مصر، وصاحب الأنهار والنعم

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p58#2/r3.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p58#2/r3.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p58#2/r3.claim: Egypt here stretches from the Sea of Alexandria to Aswan along the Nile.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p58#2/r3.anchor: مصر من بحر الإسكندرية إلى أسوان بطول النيل

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p58#2/r4.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p58#2/r4.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p58#2/r4.claim: The rivers are major channels branching from the Nile, including the Alexandria, Tanis, Damietta, and Ṭūlūn waterways.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p58#2/r4.anchor: الأنهار التي أشار إليها هي الخلجان الكبار الخارجة من النيل

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p58#2/r5.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p58#2/r5.speaker: سيبويه
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p58#2/r5.claim: Sībawayh takes am as a balancing conjunction: the sense is “or do you not see?”; the thing they should see is that Pharaoh is better than Moses, and lā is negative.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p58#2/r5.anchor: وقوله: أم أنا خير قال سيبويه: أم هذه المعادلة، والمعنى: أم أنتم لا تبصرون

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p58#2/r6.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p58#2/r6.speaker: فرقة
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p58#2/r6.claim: One group supplies the omitted second half, “do you see or not?” and treats “I am better” as a new assertion; afalā then functions as “why not,” with exhortative force.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p58#2/r6.anchor: وقالت فرقة: أفلا تبصرون أم لا تبصرون، ثم اقتصر على أم

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p58#2/r7.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p58#2/r7.speaker: فرقة
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p58#2/r7.claim: Another group interprets am as meaning bal, “rather.”

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p58#2/r8.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p58#2/r8.speaker: بعض الناس
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p58#2/r8.claim: Some read ammā anā khayrun; al-Farrāʾ reports this reading, and Mujāhid pauses after am before beginning anā khayrun.

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p58#2/r9.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p58#2/r9.speaker: قتادة
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p58#2/r9.claim: Qatāda says Ubayy ibn Kaʿb's codex reads “Am I better, or this one?”
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p58#2/r9.anchor: قال قتادة: وفي مصحف أبي بن كعب: «أم أنا خير أم هذا

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p320#5/r1.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p320#5/r1.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p320#5/r1.claim: The rivers ran beneath Pharaoh's palaces.

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p320#5/r2.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p320#5/r2.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p320#5/r2.claim: Pharaoh's question means, 'Can you not see my greatness and the extent of my dominion?'

KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p260/r1.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p260/r1.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p260/r1.claim: The call was staged among Pharaoh's people: he made their gatherings the setting and audience for his announcement.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p260/r1.anchor: جعلهم محلا لندائه وموقعا له . والمعنى : أنه أمر بالنداء في مجامعهم

KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p260/r2.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p260/r2.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p260/r2.claim: One possibility is that Pharaoh ordered a public announcement in their meeting places; the attribution to him resembles saying the emir cut the thief when he ordered it.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p260/r2.anchor: فأسند النداء إليه ، كقولك : قطع الأمير اللص ، إذا أمر بقطعه

KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p260/r3.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p260/r3.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p260/r3.claim: Alternatively, Pharaoh spoke loudly to the Coptic notables and the announcement then spread among the crowds.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p260/r3.anchor: يكون عنده عظماء القبط ، فيرفع صوته بذلك فيما بينهم ، ثم ينشر عنه في جموع القبط

KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p260/r4.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p260/r4.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p260/r4.claim: The rivers are branches of the Nile, chiefly four: the River of the King, Tulun, Damietta, and Tinnis.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p260/r4.anchor: يعني أنهار النيل ومعظمهما أربعة : نهر الملك ، ونهر طولون ، ونهر دمياط ، ونهر تنيس

KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p260/r5.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p260/r5.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p260/r5.claim: Some said the rivers flowed beneath Pharaoh's palace because of its height.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p260/r5.anchor: قيل : كانت تجري تحت قصره . وقيل : تحت سريره لارتفاعه

KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p260/r6.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p260/r6.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p260/r6.claim: Another explanation places the rivers before Pharaoh in his gardens and orchards.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p260/r6.anchor: وقيل : بين يدي في جناني وبساتيني

KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p260/r7.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p260/r7.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p260/r7.claim: The conjunction can coordinate the rivers with Egypt's kingdom, while tajrī is a circumstantial accusative; alternatively, the conjunction introduces a circumstantial clause with the demonstrative as subject.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p260/r7.anchor: ويجوز أن تكون الواو عاطفة للأنهار على ملك مصر . وتجري : نصب على الحال منها

KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p260/r8.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p260/r8.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p260/r8.claim: Pharaoh's pride at Egypt's dominion and his effort to broadcast its grandeur expose the absurdity of aspiring to divinity.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p260/r8.anchor: كيف ارتقت إلى دعوة الربوبية همة من تعظم بملك مصر ، وعجب الناس من مدى عظمته

KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p260/r9.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p260/r9.speaker: الرشيد
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p260/r9.claim: Al-Rashid said he would give Egypt to his lowliest servant after reading Pharaoh's boast, then appointed al-Khasib, who had been attending his ablutions.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p260/r9.anchor: وعن الرشيد : أنه لما قرأها قال : لأولينها أخس عبيدي ، فولاها الخصيب ، وكان على وضوئه

KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p260/r10.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p260/r10.speaker: عبد الله بن طاهر
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p260/r10.claim: Ibn Tahir dismissed Egypt as too insignificant to enter, recalling that Pharaoh had boasted of owning it.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p260/r10.anchor: وعن عبد الله بن طاهر أنه وليها ، فخرج إليها فلما شارفها ووقع عليها بصره قال

MAWARDI-FULL:v5p229/r1.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p229/r1.speaker: أبو مالك
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p229/r1.claim: Abu Malik takes Pharaoh’s calling his people to mean that he spoke to them.
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p229/r1.anchor: أن معنى نادى أي قال , قاله أبو مالك .

MAWARDI-FULL:v5p229/r2.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p229/r2.speaker: ابن جريج
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p229/r2.claim: Ibn Jurayj understands the phrase as Pharaoh ordering someone to call among his people.
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p229/r2.anchor: أمر من نادى في قومه , قاله ابن جريج . {

MAWARDI-FULL:v5p229/r3.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p229/r3.speaker: مجاهد
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p229/r3.claim: Mujahid identifies Pharaoh’s kingdom of Egypt with Alexandria.

MAWARDI-FULL:v5p229/r4.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p229/r4.speaker: النقاش
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p229/r4.claim: Al-Naqqash says Pharaoh ruled an area forty farsakhs by forty farsakhs.
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p229/r4.anchor: ملك منها أربعين فرسخا في مثلها , حكاه النقاش . {

MAWARDI-FULL:v5p229/r5.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p229/r5.speaker: قتادة
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p229/r5.claim: Qatada says rivers flowed beneath Pharaoh’s palace gardens.
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p229/r5.anchor: كانت جنات وأنهارا تجري من تحت قصره , قاله قتادة .

MAWARDI-FULL:v5p229/r6.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p229/r6.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p229/r6.claim: An alternative says the rivers flowed beneath Pharaoh’s throne.

MAWARDI-FULL:v5p229/r7.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p229/r7.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p229/r7.claim: Another interpretation identifies the rivers with the Nile, flowing below Pharaoh.
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p229/r7.anchor: أنه أراد النيل يجري من تحتي أي أسفل مني .

MAWARDI-FULL:v5p229/r8.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p229/r8.speaker: الضحاك
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p229/r8.claim: Al-Dahhak says the rivers are the commanders and mighty men who marched beneath Pharaoh’s banner.
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p229/r8.anchor:
القواد والجبابرة يسيرون تحت لوائي ,
قاله الضحاك .

MAWARDI-FULL:v5p229/r9.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p229/r9.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p229/r9.claim: Mawardi suggests that rivers metaphorically mean abundant, conspicuous wealth, which Pharaoh distributed to his followers.
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p229/r9.anchor: أنه أراد بالأنهار الأموال , وعبر عنها بالأنهار لكثرتها وظهورها

MAWARDI-FULL:v5p229/r10.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p229/r10.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p229/r10.claim: One reading of Pharaoh’s question asks whether his power and Moses’ weakness are not visible.
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p229/r10.anchor: أفلا تبصرون إلى قوتي وضعف موسى ؟ .

MAWARDI-FULL:v5p229/r11.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p229/r11.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p229/r11.claim: Another reading asks whether people cannot see Pharaoh’s ability to benefit them and Moses’ inability.

MAWARDI-FULL:v5p229/r12.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p229/r12.speaker: السدي
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p229/r12.claim: Al-Suddi glosses “Am I better?” as “Rather, I am better.”

NAHHAS:v4p112/r3.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v4p112/r3.speaker: author
NAHHAS:v4p112/r3.claim: One account says Pharaoh called his people together because he feared they would follow Moses after the punishment was lifted, revealing Pharaoh's inability; he asserted his own superior claim to obedience.
NAHHAS:v4p112/r3.anchor: قيل كان نداؤه كراهة أن يتبع قومه موسى صلى الله عليه وسلم لأنه لما دعا كشف عنهم العذاب فتبين عجز فرعون

NAHHAS:v4p112/r4.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v4p112/r4.speaker: author
NAHHAS:v4p112/r4.claim: Basran grammarians treat مصر as diptote because a feminine place name is formed from a masculine one; Kufa compares it to a woman named Hind and says rarity blocks declension, while nondeclension remains preferable.
NAHHAS:v4p112/r4.anchor: في موضع خفض ولم ينصرف عند البصريين لأنها مؤنثة سميت بمذكر وكذا لو سميت امرأة بزيد لم ينصرف

NAHHAS:v4p112/r5.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v4p112/r5.speaker: author
NAHHAS:v4p112/r5.claim: The Kufans argue that مصر should otherwise decline like the name Hind, but its rarity in speech prevents that; the uninflected form is preferable because comparable words are commonly feminine nouns such as بلدة.
NAHHAS:v4p112/r5.anchor: فأما الكوفيون فيذهبون إلى أن مصر بمنزلة امرأة سميت بهند فكان يجب أن ينصرف إلا أنها منعت من ذلك لقلتها في الكلام

NAHHAS:v4p112/r6.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v4p112/r6.speaker: author
NAHHAS:v4p112/r6.claim: In وهذه الأنهار تجري من تحتي, تجري may be accusative as a circumstantial clause or nominative as the predicate of هذه.
NAHHAS:v4p112/r6.anchor: تجري في موضع نصب على الحال ويجوز أن يكون في موضع رفع على خبر هذه

MUQATIL:43:51-53/r1.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:43:51-53/r1.speaker: author
MUQATIL:43:51-53/r1.claim: Pharaoh, the Copt, called to his Coptic people and boasted that Egypt was his kingdom, forty by forty farsakhs, with rivers flowing below him; “do you not see?” means “why do you not?”
MUQATIL:43:51-53/r1.anchor: قوله: { ونادى فرعون } القبطي، { في قومه } القبط، وكان نداؤه أنه { قال يقوم أليس لي ملك مصر } أربعين فرسخا في أربعين فرسخا

MUQATIL:43:51-53/r2.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:43:51-53/r2.speaker: author
MUQATIL:43:51-53/r2.claim: Pharaoh challenges whether his people have gardens and rivers like his.
MUQATIL:43:51-53/r2.anchor: { أفلا } ، يعني فهلا، { تبصرون } [آية: 51]، ألهم جنان وأنهار مثلها

NASAFI-FULL:v4p116#5/r1.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v4p116#5/r1.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v4p116#5/r1.claim: Pharaoh either personally summoned Egypt's nobles or ordered a herald to do so, as one may say the emir cut a thief when he ordered it.
NASAFI-FULL:v4p116#5/r1.anchor: نادى بنفسه عظماء القبط أو أمر مناديا فنادى كقولك قطع الأمير اللص اذا أمر بقطعه

NASAFI-FULL:v4p116#5/r2.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v4p116#5/r2.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v4p116#5/r2.claim: The phrase in his people makes them the place and audience of his call.
NASAFI-FULL:v4p116#5/r2.anchor: ﴿ في قومه ﴾ جعلهم محلا لندائه وموقعا له

NASAFI-FULL:v4p116#5/r3.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v4p116#5/r3.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v4p116#5/r3.claim: The rivers are the Nile's waterways, most notably four.
NASAFI-FULL:v4p116#5/r3.anchor: ﴿ قال يا قوم أليس لي ملك مصر وهذه الأنهار ﴾ أي أنهار النيل ومعظمها أربعة

NASAFI-FULL:v4p116#5/r4.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v4p116#5/r4.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v4p116#5/r4.claim: Under me may mean beneath Pharaoh's palace, or in front of him in his gardens.
NASAFI-FULL:v4p116#5/r4.anchor: ﴿ تجري من تحتي ﴾ من تحت قصرى وقيل بين يدى في جنائي

NASAFI-FULL:v4p116#5/r5.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v4p116#5/r5.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v4p116#5/r5.claim: One grammatical analysis coordinates the rivers with Egypt's kingdom and makes their flowing a circumstantial clause.
NASAFI-FULL:v4p116#5/r5.anchor: والواو عاطفة للانهار على ملك مصر وتجرى نصب على الحال منها

NASAFI-FULL:v4p116#5/r6.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v4p116#5/r6.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v4p116#5/r6.claim: Alternatively, the waw is circumstantial, this is a subject, the rivers describe it, and their flowing is its predicate.
NASAFI-FULL:v4p116#5/r6.anchor: أو الواو للحال واسم الاشارة مبتدأ والانهار صفة لاسم الاشارة وتجرى خبر للمبتدأ

NASAFI-FULL:v4p116#5/r7.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v4p116#5/r7.speaker: الرشيد
NASAFI-FULL:v4p116#5/r7.claim: After reading the verse, al-Rashid vowed to assign Egypt to his lowliest servant and gave it to al-Khasib, formerly his ablution attendant.
NASAFI-FULL:v4p116#5/r7.anchor: وعن الرشيد انه لما قرأها قال لاولينها اخس عبيدى فولاها الخصيب وكان خادمة على وضوئه

NASAFI-FULL:v4p116#5/r8.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v4p116#5/r8.speaker: عبدالله بن طاهر
NASAFI-FULL:v4p116#5/r8.claim: Abdullah ibn Tahir judged Egypt less worthy than Pharaoh's boast implied, then turned his horse away rather than enter it.
NASAFI-FULL:v4p116#5/r8.anchor: وعن عبدالله بن طاهر أنه وليها فخرج اليها فلما شارفها قال أهى القرية التي افتخر بها فرعون

NASAFI-FULL:v4p116#5/r9.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v4p116#5/r9.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v4p116#5/r9.claim: Pharaoh's challenge mocks Moses by contrasting his own youth and strength and wealth with Moses' weakness and poverty.

QURTUBI-FULL:43:49-51/r6.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:43:49-51/r6.speaker: أبو مالك
QURTUBI-FULL:43:49-51/r6.claim: Some say Pharaoh gathered his people because he feared they would turn to Moses after seeing the signs; “called out” means he spoke.
QURTUBI-FULL:43:49-51/r6.anchor: قيل: لما رأى تلك الآيات خاف ميل القوم إليه فجمع قومه فقال فنادى بمعنى قال قاله أبو مالك.

QURTUBI-FULL:43:51-52/r1.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:43:51-52/r1.speaker: ابن جريج
QURTUBI-FULL:43:51-52/r1.claim: Pharaoh may have ordered someone to make the announcement to his people; alternatively, he spoke loudly among Coptic dignitaries and the message spread among the people.
QURTUBI-FULL:43:51-52/r1.anchor: فيجوز أن يكون عنده عظماء القبط فرفع صوته بذلك فيما بينهم ثم ينشر عنه في جموع القبط وكأنه نودي به بينهم. وقيل: إنه أمر من ينادي في قومه قاله ابن جريج.

QURTUBI-FULL:43:51-52/r2.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:43:51-52/r2.speaker: النقاش
QURTUBI-FULL:43:51-52/r2.claim: One report says Pharaoh's Egyptian realm extended forty farsakhs by forty; another says “Egypt” means Alexandria.
QURTUBI-FULL:43:51-52/r2.anchor: قيل: إنه ملك منها أربعين فرسخا في مثلها حكاه النقاش. وقيل: أراد بالملك هنا الإسكندرية.

QURTUBI-FULL:43:51-52/r3.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:43:51-52/r3.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:43:51-52/r3.claim: The rivers are the Nile's branches, chiefly four: the River of the King, Tulun, Damietta, and Tanis.
QURTUBI-FULL:43:51-52/r3.anchor: يعني أنهار النيل، ومعظمها أربعة: نهر الملك ونهر طولون ونهر دمياط ونهر تنيس.

QURTUBI-FULL:43:51-52/r4.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:43:51-52/r4.speaker: قتادة
QURTUBI-FULL:43:51-52/r4.claim: Qatada says the rivers and gardens flowed below Pharaoh's palaces; another says they flowed beneath his throne.
QURTUBI-FULL:43:51-52/r4.anchor: قال قتادة: كانت جنانا وأنهارا تجري من تحت قصوره. وقيل: من تحت سريره.

QURTUBI-FULL:43:51-52/r5.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:43:51-52/r5.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:43:51-52/r5.claim: “Beneath me” can mean that Pharaoh's authority over the rivers was effective without an intermediary; another report says the Nile stopped flowing when he held its reins.
QURTUBI-FULL:43:51-52/r5.anchor: وقيل: «من تحتي» أي تصرفي نافذ فيها من غير صانع. وقيل: كان إذا أمسك عنانه أمسك النيل عن الجري.

QURTUBI-FULL:43:51-52/r6.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:43:51-52/r6.speaker: القشيري
QURTUBI-FULL:43:51-52/r6.claim: Al-Qushayri says supernatural wonders may appear through someone claiming divinity, because a miracle is not needed to distinguish God from a false god.
QURTUBI-FULL:43:51-52/r6.anchor: قال القشيري: ويجوز ظهور خوارق العادة على مدعي الربوبية إذ لا حاجة في تمييز الإله من غير الإله إلى فعل خارق للعادة.

QURTUBI-FULL:43:51-52/r7.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:43:51-52/r7.speaker: الضحاك
QURTUBI-FULL:43:51-52/r7.claim: Al-Dahhak says the “rivers” were commanders, chiefs, and tyrants marching beneath Pharaoh's banner.

QURTUBI-FULL:43:51-52/r8.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:43:51-52/r8.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:43:51-52/r8.claim: Another interpretation takes rivers as abundant, conspicuous wealth; Pharaoh says it flowed beneath him because he distributed it to followers, using wealth to entice them.
QURTUBI-FULL:43:51-52/r8.anchor: وقيل: أراد بالأنهار الأموال، وعبر عنها بالأنهار لكثرتها وظهورها. وقوله: { تجري من تحتي } أي أفرقها على من يتبعني

QURTUBI-FULL:43:51-52/r9.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:43:51-52/r9.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:43:51-52/r9.claim: “Do you not see?” means recognize Pharaoh's greatness and power and Moses' weakness, or Pharaoh's ability to spend on them and Moses' inability.
QURTUBI-FULL:43:51-52/r9.anchor: عظمتي وقوتي وضعف موسى. وقيل قدرتي على نفقتكم وعجز موسى.

QURTUBI-FULL:43:51-52/r10.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:43:51-52/r10.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:43:51-52/r10.claim: The conjunction may coordinate the rivers with Egypt's kingdom, with “flowing” a circumstantial clause, or introduce a circumstantial sentence with the demonstrative as subject and “rivers” as its modifier.
QURTUBI-FULL:43:51-52/r10.anchor: والواو في «وهذه» يجوز أن تكون عاطفة للأنهار على «ملك مصر» و «تجري» نصب على الحال منها. ويجوز أن تكون واو الحال

QURTUBI-FULL:43:51-52/r11.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:43:51-52/r11.speaker: أهل المدينة والبزي وأبو عمرو
QURTUBI-FULL:43:51-52/r11.claim: These readers pronounce the yāʾ in “taḥtī” with fatḥ; the remaining readers make it still.
QURTUBI-FULL:43:51-52/r11.anchor: وفتح الياء من «تحتي» أهل المدينة والبزي وأبو عمرو، وأسكن الباقون.

QURTUBI-FULL:43:51-52/r12.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:43:51-52/r12.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:43:51-52/r12.claim: Al-Rashid reportedly promised Egypt to the best of his servants after reciting the verse, and gave it to al-Khasib, who had been assisting him with ablutions.
QURTUBI-FULL:43:51-52/r12.anchor: وعن الرشيد أنه لما قرأها قال: لأولينها أحسن عبيدي، فولاها الخصيب، وكان على وضوئه.

QURTUBI-FULL:43:51-52/r13.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:43:51-52/r13.speaker: عبد الله بن طاهر
QURTUBI-FULL:43:51-52/r13.claim: When appointed governor, Abd Allah ibn Tahir turned back as he approached Egypt, judging it beneath the boast Pharaoh had made about owning it.
QURTUBI-FULL:43:51-52/r13.anchor: وعن عبد الله بن طاهر أنه وليها فخرج إليها فلما شارفها ووقع عليها بصره قال: أهذه القرية التي افتخر بها فرعون

STUDYQURAN:43:intro/r16.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:43:intro/r16.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:43:intro/r16.claim: The idolaters’ opposition to the Prophet is likened to Pharaoh and his notables opposing Moses.
STUDYQURAN:43:intro/r16.anchor: the opposition of the idolaters to the Prophet is likened to the opposition of Pharaoh and his “notables” toward Moses (vv.46–56)

STUDYQURAN:43:46/r15.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:43:46/r15.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:43:46/r15.claim: Pharaoh's claim about the streams displays haughtiness: from the Quranic perspective, God alone makes water flow.
STUDYQURAN:43:46/r15.anchor: Pharaoh’s invocation of the streams running beneath his feet as a sign of his sovereignty demonstrates both his haughtiness

STUDYQURAN:43:46/r16.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:43:46/r16.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:43:46/r16.claim: Pharaoh is ignorant of how God may grant respite and remove worldly blessings at any moment.
STUDYQURAN:43:46/r16.anchor: and his ignorance, since the Quran warns that God grants respite for a while, but can remove such blessings at any moment

TAB-FULL:v20p610#3/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v20p610#3/r1.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v20p610#3/r1.claim: Pharaoh called to his Egyptian people and boasted that Egypt belonged to him and that its rivers flowed before him through gardens.
TAB-FULL:v20p610#3/r1.anchor: عن قتادة، {وهذه الأنهار تجري من تحتي} [الزخرف: 51] قال: «كانت لهم جنات وأنهار ماء»

TAB-FULL:v20p610#3/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v20p610#3/r2.speaker: قتادة
TAB-FULL:v20p610#3/r2.claim: Qatāda says Pharaoh's people had gardens and rivers of water.
TAB-FULL:v20p610#3/r2.anchor: عن قتادة، {وهذه الأنهار تجري من تحتي} [الزخرف: 51] قال: «كانت لهم جنات وأنهار ماء»

TAB-FULL:v20p610#3/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v20p610#3/r3.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v20p610#3/r3.claim: Pharaoh taunted his people to compare his worldly prosperity with Moses' poverty and speech impediment, using his kingdom and blessings to persuade them that Moses could not be truthful.
TAB-FULL:v20p610#3/r3.anchor: أفلا تبصرون أيها القوم ما أنا فيه من النعيم والخير، وما فيه موسى من الفقر وعي اللسان

TAB-FULL:v20p610#3/r4.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v20p610#3/r4.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v20p610#3/r4.claim: Pharaoh's worldly power was God's way of luring him on; he foolishly credited his wealth to his own power and used it to demean Moses and mislead his ignorant people about God's signs.
TAB-FULL:v20p610#3/r4.anchor: افتخر بملكه مصر عدو الله، وما قد مكن له من الدنيا استدراجا من الله له

SAMIN-DURR:43:51/r1.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:43:51/r1.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:43:51/r1.claim: هذه may begin a circumstantial clause, with الأنهار an adjective or apposition, تجري its predicate, and the clause circumstantial of لي.
SAMIN-DURR:43:51/r1.anchor: أحدهما: أن تكون مبتدأة، والواو للحال. والأنهار صفة لاسم الإشارة، أو عطف بيان.

SAMIN-DURR:43:51/r2.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:43:51/r2.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:43:51/r2.claim: Alternatively, هذه coordinates with ملك مصر and تجري is circumstantial, so Pharaoh claims both kingship and rivers flowing beneath him.
SAMIN-DURR:43:51/r2.anchor: أي: أليس ملك مصر وهذه الأنهار جارية أي: الشيئان.

SAMIN-DURR:43:51/r3.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:43:51/r3.speaker: العامة
SAMIN-DURR:43:51/r3.claim: The common second-person تبصرون addresses Pharaoh's audience; its omitted object is his dominion and grandeur.
SAMIN-DURR:43:51/r3.anchor: وفي قراءة العامة المفعول محذوف أي: تبصرون ملكي وعظمتي.

SAMIN-DURR:43:51/r4.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:43:51/r4.speaker: عيسى
SAMIN-DURR:43:51/r4.claim: Isa reads تبصروني with kasra on nūn.
SAMIN-DURR:43:51/r4.anchor: وقرأ عيسى بكسر النون أي: تبصروني.

SAMIN-DURR:43:51/r5.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:43:51/r5.speaker: فهد بن الصقر
SAMIN-DURR:43:51/r5.claim: Fahd ibn al-Saqr reads third-person يبصرون, either shifting from direct address or referring back to Moses's people.
SAMIN-DURR:43:51/r5.anchor: وقرأ فهد بن الصقر " يبصرون " بياء الغيبة: إما على الالتفات من الخطاب إلى الغيبة

TABATABAI:43:47-51/r1.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:43:47-51/r1.speaker: author
TABATABAI:43:47-51/r1.claim: The opening links Quraysh's preference for a wealthy notable over the Prophet with Pharaoh's boast, showing how arrogance before clear revelation ends in drowning.
TABATABAI:43:47-51/r1.anchor: فرجحوا الرجل على النبي صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم بكثرة ماله مثل لهم بقصة موسى عليه السلام وفرعون وقومه

TABATABAI:43:47-51/r17.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:43:47-51/r17.speaker: author
TABATABAI:43:47-51/r17.claim: Pharaoh called to his people while he was among them; the separate قال answers the implied question, What did he say?
TABATABAI:43:47-51/r17.anchor: أي ناداهم وهو بينهم، وفصل { قال } لكونه في موضع جواب السؤال كأنه قيل فماذا قال؟

TABATABAI:43:51-53/r1.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:43:51-53/r1.speaker: author
TABATABAI:43:51-53/r1.claim: From beneath me may mean beneath Pharaoh's palace or beneath its elevated garden containing the palace.
TABATABAI:43:51-53/r1.anchor: أي من تحت قصري أو من بستاني الذي فيه قصري المرتفع العالي البناء

TABATABAI:43:51-53/r2.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:43:51-53/r2.speaker: author
TABATABAI:43:51-53/r2.claim: The rivers are the Nile's branches.

TABATABAI:43:51-53/r3.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:43:51-53/r3.speaker: author
TABATABAI:43:51-53/r3.claim: The clause about the rivers may be circumstantial, or these rivers may be coordinated with Egypt's kingdom, with their running clause circumstantial.
TABATABAI:43:51-53/r3.anchor: والجملة أعني قوله و { هذه الأنهار } الخ، حالية أو { وهذه الأنهار } معطوف على { ملك مصر }

TABATABAI:43:51-53/r4.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:43:51-53/r4.speaker: author
TABATABAI:43:51-53/r4.claim: The running clause is circumstantial to the rivers.
TABATABAI:43:51-53/r4.anchor: وقوله { تجري من تحتي } حال من الأنهار

TABATABAI:43:51-53/r5.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:43:51-53/r5.speaker: author
TABATABAI:43:51-53/r5.claim: Do you not see repeats the force of the earlier question, Is not Egypt's kingdom mine?
TABATABAI:43:51-53/r5.anchor: وقوله { أفلا تبصرون } في معنى تكرير الاستفهام السابق في قوله { أليس لي ملك مصر } الخ

TABRISI:43:46-51/r14.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:43:46-51/r14.speaker: author
TABRISI:43:46-51/r14.claim: When Moses’ influence visibly increased and Pharaoh feared for his kingdom, he addressed the assembled people deceptively.
TABRISI:43:46-51/r14.anchor: معناه أنه لما رأى أمر موسى يزيد على الأيام ظهورا واعتلاء خاف على مملكته فأظهر الخداع

TABRISI:43:46-51/r15.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:43:46-51/r15.speaker: author
TABRISI:43:46-51/r15.claim: Pharaoh’s claim to own Egypt means he could control it as he wished, displaying his power and wealth.
TABRISI:43:46-51/r15.anchor: أتصرف فيها كما أشاء أراد بذلك إظهار بسطته في الملك والمال

TABRISI:43:46-51/r16.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:43:46-51/r16.speaker: author
TABRISI:43:46-51/r16.claim: The rivers include the Nile and others; flowing from beneath him means under his command.
TABRISI:43:46-51/r16.anchor: مثل النيل وغيرها { تجري من تحتي } أي من تحت أمري

TABRISI:43:51-54/r1.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:43:51-54/r1.speaker: author
TABRISI:43:51-54/r1.claim: Alternatively, the rivers flowed below Pharaoh’s palace, which overlooked them.
TABRISI:43:51-54/r1.anchor: وقيل: إنها كانت تجري تحت قصره وهو مشرف عليها

TABRISI:43:51-54/r2.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:43:51-54/r2.speaker: author
TABRISI:43:51-54/r2.claim: Do you not see means Pharaoh points to his great kingdom and power and Moses’ weakness.
TABRISI:43:51-54/r2.anchor: هذا الملك العظيم وقوتي وضعف موسى

ZAJJAJ:v4p414/r3.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v4p414/r3.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v4p414/r3.claim: مصر here is the familiar city of Egypt, grammatically masculine although the word for city is usually feminine.
ZAJJAJ:v4p414/r3.anchor:
مصر " ههنا يعنى بها مدينة مصر المعروفة، فمصر مذكر سمي به مؤنث
لأن المدينة الغالب عليها التأنيث

ZAJJAJ:v4p414/r4.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v4p414/r4.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v4p414/r4.claim: It is possible to construe مصر as a country name, but Zajjāj finds this unlikely because بلد usually denotes a region containing several major cities.
ZAJJAJ:v4p414/r4.anchor:
وقد يجوز ملك مصر، يذهب به إلى أن
مصر اسم لبلد، وهذا فيه بعد من قبل أن أكثر ما يستعمل البلد لما يضم مدنا
كبيرة

ZAJJAJ:v4p414/r5.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v4p414/r5.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v4p414/r5.claim: If مصر is treated as a country name, Basran grammarians all allow it to be fully declinable.
ZAJJAJ:v4p414/r5.anchor: ويجوز أن تصرف مصرا إذا جعلته اسما لبلد عند جميع النحويين من البصريين

ZAJJAJ:v4p415/r1.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v4p415/r1.speaker: سيبويه والخليل
ZAJJAJ:v4p415/r1.claim: Sībawayh and al-Khalīl attach أنا in أم أنا خير to the preceding أفلا تبصرون, since أم أنا خير means أم تبصرون: are you not seeing, or do you see that I am better?
ZAJJAJ:v4p415/r1.anchor: قال سيبويه والخليل عطف " أنا " ب (أم) على قوله (أفلا تبصرون)

THALABI:v8p339/r1.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v8p339/r1.speaker: author
THALABI:v8p339/r1.claim: The Nile has four principal branches named the River of the King, Tulun, Damietta, and Tanis.
THALABI:v8p339/r1.anchor: يعني أنهار النيل ومعظمها أربعة: نهر الملك، ونهر طولون، ونهر دمياط، ونهر تنيس

THALABI:v8p339/r2.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v8p339/r2.speaker: author
THALABI:v8p339/r2.claim: “Flow beneath me” means the rivers run before Pharaoh among his gardens and orchards; Ibn Abbas says around him, Ata says in his possession and dominion, and Hasan says by his command.
THALABI:v8p339/r2.anchor: تجري من تحتي بين يدي وجناتي وبساتيني، وقال ابن عباس: حولي

THALABI:v8p339/r3.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v8p339/r3.speaker: عطاء
THALABI:v8p339/r3.claim: Ata interprets the rivers running beneath Pharaoh as being in his control and possession.

THALABI:v8p339/r4.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v8p339/r4.speaker: الحسن
THALABI:v8p339/r4.claim: Hasan interprets their flowing as happening by Pharaoh's command.

THALABI:v8p339/r5.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v8p339/r5.speaker: author
THALABI:v8p339/r5.claim: Most commentators take “am” as “rather,” while al-Farra and a group of semantic grammarians pause at “am”; the author also explains an ellipsis before Pharaoh begins “I am better.”
THALABI:v8p339/r5.anchor: أفلا تبصرون أم أنا خير بل أنا بخير. (أم) بمعنى بل، وليس بحرف على قول أكثر المفسرين

THALABI:v8p339/r6.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v8p339/r6.speaker: الفراء
THALABI:v8p339/r6.claim: Al-Farra and other semantic grammarians place a pause at “am,” treating it as the end of the preceding statement.
THALABI:v8p339/r6.anchor: وقال الفراء: وقوم من أهل المعاني الوقوف على قوله (أم) ، وعنده تمام الكلام

THALABI:v8p339/r7.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v8p339/r7.speaker: author
THALABI:v8p339/r7.claim: Pharaoh calls Moses lowly, weak, and contemptible; “he can hardly make himself clear” refers to Moses' speech impediment, stutter, and tongue knot.
THALABI:v8p339/r7.anchor: فقال: أنا خير من هذا الذي هو مهين ضعيف حقير يعني موسى (عليه السلام) . ولا يكاد يبين يفصح بكلامه وحجته، لعيه ولعقدته والرنة التي في لسانه

THALABI:v8p339/r8.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v8p339/r8.speaker: الحسن ويعقوب وأبو حاتم وحفص
THALABI:v8p339/r8.claim: Hasan, Yaqub, Abu Hatim, and Hafs read “aswira,” while Ubay reads “asāwir,” Ibn Masud “asāwīr,” and the common reading “asāwira” is a plural of a plural.
THALABI:v8p339/r8.anchor: قرأ الحسن ويعقوب وأبو حاتم وحفص أسورة على جمع السوار، وقرأ أبي: أساور

THALABI:v8p339#2/r1.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v8p339#2/r1.speaker: أبو عمرو بن العلاء
THALABI:v8p339#2/r1.claim: Abu Amr says “asāwira,” “asāwir,” and “asāwīr” share the singular “asāwir,” a dialectal form for bracelet.
THALABI:v8p339#2/r1.anchor: وقال أبو عمرو بن العلاء: واحد الأساورة والأساور والأساوير أساور، وهي لغة في السوار

THALABI:v8p339#2/r2.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v8p339#2/r2.speaker: مجاهد
THALABI:v8p339#2/r2.claim: Mujahid says a man invested with leadership received a gold bracelet and necklace as its insignia; Pharaoh asks why Moses' Lord did not give him gold bracelets.
THALABI:v8p339#2/r2.anchor: قال مجاهد: كانوا إذا استودوا رجلا سوروه بسوار، وطوقوه بطوق من ذهب يكون ذلك دلالة لسيادته

THALABI:v8p339#2/r3.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v8p339#2/r3.speaker: author
THALABI:v8p339#2/r3.claim: “Accompanied” angels means following one another in a group, walking with Moses as witnesses for him.
THALABI:v8p339#2/r3.anchor: أو جاء معه الملائكة مقترنين متابعين يقارن بعضهم بعضا يمشون معه شاهدين له

WAHIDI-BASIT:v20p56/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v20p56/r1.speaker: المفسرون
WAHIDI-BASIT:v20p56/r1.claim: The rivers Pharaoh boasts of are the Nile's rivers.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v20p56/r1.anchor: يعني: أنهار النيل، في قول المفسرين

WAHIDI-BASIT:v20p56/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v20p56/r2.speaker: مقاتل
WAHIDI-BASIT:v20p56/r2.claim: Muqatil interprets “beneath me” as below him, meaning beneath his palaces.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v20p56/r2.anchor: قال مقاتل: يعني: أسفل مني (¬1)، كأنه أراد من تحت قصوره

WAHIDI-BASIT:v20p56/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v20p56/r3.speaker: الكلبي
WAHIDI-BASIT:v20p56/r3.claim: Al-Kalbi interprets the rivers as flowing around Pharaoh.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v20p56/r4.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v20p56/r4.speaker: قتادة
WAHIDI-BASIT:v20p56/r4.claim: Qatada says the rivers flowed before Pharaoh in his gardens.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v20p56/r4.anchor: وقال قتادة: بين يدي في جناتي

WAHIDI-BASIT:v20p56/r5.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v20p56/r5.speaker: الحسن وعطاء
WAHIDI-BASIT:v20p56/r5.claim: Al-Hasan says the rivers flowed by Pharaoh's command; Ata says they were under his control and ownership.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v20p56/r5.anchor: وقال الحسن: بأمر (¬4)، وعلى هذا معناه: تجري تحت أمري، وهو معنى قول عطاء: في قبضتي وملكي

WAHIDI-BASIT:v20p56/r6.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v20p56/r6.speaker: ابن عباس
WAHIDI-BASIT:v20p56/r6.claim: Ibn Abbas says Pharaoh asks whether they see his blessings and wealth compared with Moses' poverty, as the enemy boasts of his kingdom.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v20p56/r6.anchor: قال ابن عباس: أفلا تبصرون ما أنا فيه من النعم والخير، وما فيه موسى من الفقر، افتخر عدو الله بملكه

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:43:48-53/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:43:48-53/r3.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:43:48-53/r3.claim: Pharaoh says the rivers flow beneath him by his command.
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:43:48-53/r3.anchor: وهذه الأنهار تجري من تحتي } بأمري. وقيل: من تحت قصوري.

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:43:48-53/r4.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:43:48-53/r4.speaker: قيل
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:43:48-53/r4.claim: An alternative says the rivers flow beneath Pharaoh's palaces.
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:43:48-53/r4.anchor: وهذه الأنهار تجري من تحتي } بأمري. وقيل: من تحت قصوري.

BURHAN:v2p334/r6.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v2p334/r6.speaker: author
BURHAN:v2p334/r6.claim: Pharaoh's question about owning Egypt exemplifies affirmation coupled with boasting.
BURHAN:v2p334/r6.anchor: الثاني الاثبات مع الافتخار كقوله تعالى عن فرعون

BURHAN:v4p181/r7.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v4p181/r7.speaker: الفراء وقوم من أهل المعاني
BURHAN:v4p181/r7.claim: Al-Farra and some grammarians stop at أم and supply an omitted question before أنا خير; the author says this makes أم disconnected, unlike the alternative connected parsing.
BURHAN:v4p181/r7.anchor: وقال الفراء وقوم من أهل المعاني الوقف على قوله أم

BURHAN:v4p181/r8.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v4p181/r8.speaker: أبو زيد
BURHAN:v4p181/r8.claim: Abu Zayd calls أم redundant, supplying the sense: do you not see that I am better than him?
BURHAN:v4p181/r8.anchor: قال أبو زيد إنها زائدة وإن التقدير

BURHAN:v4p181/r9.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v4p181/r9.speaker: author
BURHAN:v4p181/r9.claim: The familiar analysis is disconnected أم: after asserting his claim, Pharaoh doubts that they see and asks whether he is better.
BURHAN:v4p181/r9.anchor: والمشهور أنها منقطعة لأنه لا يسألهم عن استواء علمه

BURHAN:v4p181/r10.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v4p181/r10.speaker: ابن طاهر
BURHAN:v4p181/r10.claim: Ibn Tahir asked his teacher Ibn al-Rammak why Sibawayh did not parse أم as connected; the teacher stayed silent, then resumed teaching after Ibn Tahir reconciled with him.
BURHAN:v4p181/r10.anchor: وسأل ابن طاهر شيخه أبا القاسم بن الرماك

BURHAN:v1p315/r1.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v1p315/r1.speaker: author
BURHAN:v1p315/r1.claim: The poem offered as an example of this rhetorical style answers estrangement, betrayal, and claims of self-sufficiency with reciprocal replies.
BURHAN:v1p315/r1.anchor: ومما تجد من هذا الطراز قول بعضهم

BURHAN:v4p183/r1.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v4p183/r1.speaker: author
BURHAN:v4p183/r1.claim: One reading takes Pharaoh first to ask whether his people cannot see, then to break off and ask whether he is better than Moses; the initial negative question also makes best sense if the following أم is disjunctive.
BURHAN:v4p183/r1.anchor: والجواب من وجهين أحدهما انه ظن أنهم لا يبصرون فاستفهم عن ذلك ثم ظن أنهم يبصرون

BURHAN:v4p183/r2.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v4p183/r2.speaker: الواحدي
BURHAN:v4p183/r2.claim: Al-Wahidi allows أم يريدون كيدا to be connected to a preceding rebuttal or to begin a new question; أليس لي ملك مصر followed by أم أنا خير is intermediate in wording but begins a new question in meaning.
BURHAN:v4p183/r2.anchor: قال الواحدي إن شئت جعلت قبله استفهاما رد عليه وهو قوله

BURHAN:v4p183/r3.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v4p183/r3.speaker: أبو البقاء
BURHAN:v4p183/r3.claim: Abu al-Baqa's analysis, endorsed by Zarkashi, makes أم disjunctive here because there is no interrogative hamza in the preceding clause for it to coordinate with.
BURHAN:v4p183/r3.anchor: والتحقيق ما قاله أبو البقاء إنها هاهنا منقطعة إذ ليس في الكلام همزة تقع موقعها وموقع أم

ITQAN:v3p214/r6.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v3p214/r6.speaker: author
ITQAN:v3p214/r6.claim: Pharaoh’s question about owning Egypt exemplifies interrogation used for self-praise.
ITQAN:v3p214/r6.anchor: السابع الافتخار نحو ﴿ أليس لي ملك مصر ﴾

ITQAN:v4p381/r1.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v4p381/r1.speaker: author
ITQAN:v4p381/r1.claim: Dhu al-Qarnayn is variously identified as Alexander, Abdullah ibn al-Dahhak ibn Saʿd, al-Mundhir ibn Maʾ al-Samaʾ, or al-Saʿb ibn Qarin ibn al-Hamal; Ibn Askar transmits two of these names.
ITQAN:v4p381/r1.anchor: ومنها ذو القرنين واسمه إسكندر وقيل عبد الله بن الضحاك بن سعد وقيل المنذر بن ماء السماء وقيل الصعب بن قرين بن الهمال حكاهما ابن عسكر

ITQAN:v4p381/r2.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v4p381/r2.speaker: author
ITQAN:v4p381/r2.claim: One explanation of Dhu al-Qarnayn is that he reached the two ends of the earth, east and west.
ITQAN:v4p381/r2.anchor: ولقب ذا القرنين لأنه بلغ قرني الأرض المشرق والمغرب

ITQAN:v4p381/r3.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v4p381/r3.speaker: author
ITQAN:v4p381/r3.claim: Another explanation is that he ruled Persia and Rome.

ITQAN:v4p381/r4.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v4p381/r4.speaker: author
ITQAN:v4p381/r4.claim: Another explanation is that he had two locks or horns on his head.
ITQAN:v4p381/r4.anchor: وقيل كان على رأسه قرنان أي ذؤابتان

ITQAN:v4p381/r5.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v4p381/r5.speaker: author
ITQAN:v4p381/r5.claim: Another explanation is that he wore two horns made of gold.
ITQAN:v4p381/r5.anchor: وقيل كان له قرنان من ذهب

ITQAN:v4p381/r6.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v4p381/r6.speaker: author
ITQAN:v4p381/r6.claim: Another explanation is that the sides of his head were copper.
ITQAN:v4p381/r6.anchor: وقيل كانت صفحتا رأسه من نحاس

ITQAN:v4p381/r7.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v4p381/r7.speaker: author
ITQAN:v4p381/r7.claim: Another explanation is that he had two small horns hidden by his turban.
ITQAN:v4p381/r7.anchor: وقيل كان على رأسه قرنان صغيران تواريهما العمامة

ITQAN:v4p381/r8.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v4p381/r8.speaker: author
ITQAN:v4p381/r8.claim: Another explanation is that he was struck on one horn and died, was raised, and was struck on the other.
ITQAN:v4p381/r8.anchor: وقيل إنه ضرب على قرنه فمات ثم بعثه الله فضربوه على قرنه الآخر

ITQAN:v4p381/r9.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v4p381/r9.speaker: author
ITQAN:v4p381/r9.claim: Another explanation is that he was noble on both sides of his family.

ITQAN:v4p381/r10.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v4p381/r10.speaker: author
ITQAN:v4p381/r10.claim: Another explanation is that two generations of people died out during his lifetime.
ITQAN:v4p381/r10.anchor: وقيل أنه انقرض في وقته قرنان من الناس وهو حي

ITQAN:v4p381/r11.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v4p381/r11.speaker: author
ITQAN:v4p381/r11.claim: Another explanation is that he was given knowledge of the outward and inward.
ITQAN:v4p381/r11.anchor: وقيل لأنه أعطي علم الظاهر وعلم الباطن

ITQAN:v4p381/r12.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v4p381/r12.speaker: author
ITQAN:v4p381/r12.claim: Another explanation is that he entered the regions of light and darkness.

ITQAN:v4p381/r13.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v4p381/r13.speaker: author
ITQAN:v4p381/r13.claim: Pharaoh is identified as al-Walid ibn Musʿab, with the kunyas Abu al-Abbas, Abu al-Walid, or Abu Murra also reported.
ITQAN:v4p381/r13.anchor: ومنها فرعون واسمه الوليد بن مصعب وكنيته أبو العباس وقيل أبو الوليد وقيل أبو مرة

ITQAN:v4p381/r14.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v4p381/r14.speaker: قائلون
ITQAN:v4p381/r14.claim: Some say Pharaoh was a title for every ruler of Egypt.
ITQAN:v4p381/r14.anchor: وقيل إن فرعون لقب لكل من ملك مصر

ITQAN:v4p381/r15.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v4p381/r15.speaker: مجاهد
ITQAN:v4p381/r15.claim: Ibn Abi Hatim transmits Mujahid's view that Pharaoh was Persian, from Istakhr.
ITQAN:v4p381/r15.anchor: أخرج ابن أبي حاتم عن مجاهد قال كان فرعون فارسيا من أهل إصطخر
