ITQAN:v4p381/r16.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v4p381/r16.speaker: author
ITQAN:v4p381/r16.claim: Tubbaʿ is said to have been named Asʿad ibn Maliki Karib; he was called Tubbaʿ because many people followed him.
ITQAN:v4p381/r16.anchor: ومنها تبع قيل كان اسمه أسعد بن ملكي كرب وسمى تبعا لكثرة من تبعه

ITQAN:v4p381/r17.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v4p381/r17.speaker: قائلون
ITQAN:v4p381/r17.claim: Another view treats Tubbaʿ as a title for Yemen's kings, each following his predecessor like a caliph succeeding another.
ITQAN:v4p381/r17.anchor: وقيل إنه لقب ملوك اليمن سمي كل واحد منهما تبعا أي يتبع صاحبه كالخليفة يخلف غيره

BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p377/r2.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p377/r2.speaker: author
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p377/r2.claim: In Pharaoh's speech, the rivers serve as a boast about his worldly power.
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p377/r2.anchor: أو على وجه المباهاة بها في الحكاية عن فرعون

BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p40/r1.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p40/r1.speaker: author
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p40/r1.claim: From the beginning of the mission, Qur'anic inimitability was apparent to Quraysh; Arabic speakers with an innate command of their language recognized that it was not human speech.
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p40/r1.anchor: أدركت قريش ما لهذا البيان القرآني من إعجاز لا يملك أي عربي يجد حسَّ لغته وذوقها الأصيل

BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p40/r2.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p40/r2.speaker: author
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p40/r2.claim: Quraysh's pagan leaders tried to stop visiting Arab tribes from hearing the Qur'an at pilgrimage season, warning that its 'magic' divided families and clans.
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p40/r2.anchor: ترصدوا لها عند مداخل مكة، وأخذوا بسبل الناس لا يمر بهم أحد إلا حذروه من الإصغاء

BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p40/r3.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p40/r3.speaker: author
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p40/r3.claim: The author says some of Islam's fiercest opponents who heard Qur'anic verses laid down their arms and submitted, convinced the words were not human.
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p40/r3.anchor: فألقى سلاحه مصدقا ومبايعًا، عن يقين بأن مثل هذه الآيات ليست من قول البشر

BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p40/r4.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p40/r4.speaker: author
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p40/r4.claim: A report says Umar left one evening with his sword to kill Muhammad at a gathering near al-Safa; a man he met challenged him to consider what Banu Abd Manaf would do and urged him to return to his family.
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p40/r4.anchor: حدثوا أن عمر بن الخطاب خرج ذات مساء متوشحا سيفه يريد رسول الله

BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p60/r1.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p60/r1.speaker: author
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p60/r1.claim: Quraysh resisted a prophet who rejected ancestral religion and unsettled inherited social order, as well as Mecca's religious and commercial privileges and markets.
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p60/r1.anchor: جاء يسفه أحلامهم وينسخ دين آبائهم ويقوض أوضاعاً سائدة راسخة

BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p60/r2.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p60/r2.speaker: author
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p60/r2.claim: Muhammad did not bring the kind of sign earlier messengers brought; he recited the Arabic Qur'an, which Quraysh knew to be inimitable.
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p60/r2.anchor: ولم يأتهم "محمد بن عبد الله" بآية من مثل ما أتى المرسَلون قبله. وتلا عليهم ما أوحى إليه من هذا القرآن العربي المبين

BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p60/r3.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p60/r3.speaker: author
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p60/r3.claim: Quraysh had never known Muhammad to lie and did not doubt his trustworthiness, sound judgment, or character, yet the dispute pushed them toward accusations they knew were false.
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p60/r3.anchor: وما عهدوا على "محمد بين عبد الله" كذباً قط، ولا ارتابوا في أمانته ورجاحة عقله وكرم خلقه

BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p60/r4.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p60/r4.speaker: author
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p60/r4.claim: The author distinguishes Quraysh's actual judgment of the Qur'anic miracle from polemical claims made in stubborn opposition to turn Arabs away from the message.
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p60/r4.anchor: ينبغي أن نفرق في موقفهم من المعجزة، بين حقيقة رأيهم فيها، وبين ما انساقوا إليه من دعاوى جدلية

BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p60/r5.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p60/r5.speaker: author
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p60/r5.claim: The Quraysh privately recognized that the Qur'an was neither poetry, magic, nor soothsaying, and knew it differed from every kind of human speech.
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p60/r5.anchor: مع إقرارهم فيما بينهم وبين أنفسهم بأنه ليس شيئاً من ذلك كله، ويقينهم أنه غير ما عرفوا من كلام البشر

NASHR:v2p370/r1.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v2p370/r1.speaker: المدنيان وأبو عمرو والبزي
NASHR:v2p370/r1.claim: The two Madinans, Abu Amr, and al-Bazzi open the yāʾ of من تحتي; al-Karazini uniquely reports it through al-Shatwi from Ibn Shanabudh from Qunbul.
NASHR:v2p370/r1.anchor: من تحتي أفلا فتحها المدنيان، وأبو عمرو والبزي
